title: ALISTA: Analytic Weights Are As Good As Learned Weights in LISTA

citations.claim: Liu et al. proposed Analytic LISTA (ALISTA), which computes the weight matrix in LISTA analytically via a data-free coherence minimization problem, leaving only layer-wise step sizes and thresholds to be learned from data.
ALISTA reduces the number of learnable parameters from O(KNM + K) in LISTA-CPSS to O(K), where K is the number of layers, by tying the weight matrix across all layers and computing it analytically.

ALISTA decomposes training into a data-free analytic optimization stage that solves a convex quadratic program for the weight matrix, followed by a lightweight data-driven stage that learns only per-layer step sizes and thresholds.
Liu et al. proved that ALISTA retains the optimal linear convergence rate established by Chen et al. (2018) despite computing weight matrices analytically rather than learning them.
ALISTA established a minimum-coherence criterion between the weight matrix and the dictionary, formalized as minimizing the Frobenius norm of W^T D subject to unit diagonal constraints.
Liu et al. proved a recovery error lower bound showing that LISTA convergence cannot be faster than linear rate, confirming that the analytically computed parameters are optimal in convergence order.
ALISTA demonstrated that learning only scalar parameters (step sizes and thresholds) per layer achieves performance comparable to full LISTA models that learn entire weight matrices.
Liu et al. extended ALISTA to convolutional sparse coding by exploiting circular convolution approximations to efficiently solve the convolutional coherence minimization problem.

ALISTA introduced a robust training scheme that adds perturbations to the dictionary D during training, producing models with stronger robustness when the input distribution varies compared to classical LISTA.

The ALISTA framework demonstrates that the key learnable components in unfolded ISTA networks are the per-layer scalar parameters rather than the full weight matrices, providing insight into the working mechanism of LISTA.

do_not_claim: ALISTA was the first work to unfold ISTA as a neural network
ALISTA introduced the concept of algorithm unrolling
ALISTA was applied to baseline correction or chromatography
ALISTA uses deep neural network sub-modules or free-form DNNs within its layers
